observations: Photo 0 and photo 1 show the same shipping container packed with dozens of used/second-hand engines stacked on wooden shelves.
A man in a red shirt and cap is standing on the truck bed, bending into the container, apparently inspecting or marking engines.
No single engine is isolated, labeled, or shown with a readable part number, VIN tag, or sticker.
The engines are dusty, oily, and show no visible testing rig, oil pressure gauge, or running demonstration.
Photos appear to be generic bulk-stock/warehouse shots rather than a photo of one specific unit for sale.

claims.evidence: No single engine in the photos is matched to any one of these models; container shows mixed, unlabeled engines.
No shipping documents, customs paperwork, or container ID plate visible in either photo.
No video or audio of the engine running, no compression test, no specific unit shown being tested.
No odometer, service sticker, or mileage tag visible on any engine in the photos.
No close-up of seals, bolts, or valve cover to confirm it has not been disassembled.

risks.risk: Buyer cannot know which specific engine (of many models listed) they would actually receive.
risks.proof: A photo of the single engine being sold, with its block casting number or OEM tag clearly visible.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified/generic used engine, lowest tier worst case

risks.risk: Engine could be non-running, cracked block, or have internal damage not visible externally.
risks.proof: Video of the specific unit being started and run, plus a compression test reading.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for parts only

risks.risk: Mileage and history (accident, flood) cannot be verified from a bulk container shot.
risks.proof: Import/customs paperwork or dealer invoice showing mileage and origin for the specific unit.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown mileage/history, worst case

risks.risk: No proof the engine has not been opened or rebuilt with mismatched parts.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of seal tape, bolt torque marks, and valve cover gasket condition.

proof_requests: A clear photo of the exact engine being sold, separated from the pile, showing the block casting/part number.
A video of that specific engine running (cold start, idle, revving) to support 'tested and working, no knock'.
Import/customs documentation or a mileage sticker for the specific unit.
Close-up photos of seals and bolts to support 'never opened'.
response.reason: The photos show a generic container of many mixed, unlabeled used engines rather than the specific engine being offered, so it is impossible to tell which model (RX350, ES350, IS250, Camry, etc.) the buyer would actually receive.
